$f(n) = f(n-1) + f(n-2)$

This formula is based on the fact that the bug can move either one square to the right and then $n-1$ squares up, or $n-2$ squares up and then one square to the right.

We can also define a base case for the recursion:

$f(1) = 1$

This is because there is only one way to move from the lower left corner to the upper right corner on a $1 \times 1$ grid.

Using the recursive formula and base case, we can calculate the values of $f(n)$ for $n = 2, 3, 4, \ldots, 10$.

$f(2) = f(1) + f(0) = 1 + 0 = 1$

$f(3) = f(2) + f(1) = 1 + 1 = 2$

$f(4) = f(3) + f(2) = 2 + 1 = 3$

$f(5) = f(4) + f(3) = 3 + 2 = 5$

$f(6) = f(5) + f(4) = 5 + 3 = 8$

$f(7) = f(6) + f(5) = 8 + 5 = 13$

$f(8) = f(7) + f(6) = 13 + 8 = 21$

$f(9) = f(8) + f(7) = 21 + 13 = 34$

$f(10) = f(9) + f(8) = 34 + 21 = 55$

Therefore, the number of paths from the lower left corner to the upper right corner on a $10 \times 10$ grid is $N = f(10) = 55$.
